sense: of society, of living with others

evidence: Sen. Clem. 1.3.2: hominem sociāle animal commūnī bonō genitum
Sen. Ben. 5.11.5: beneficium dare sociālis rēs est
terms.comment: In this sense post-Augustan (Seneca). In Cicero and Livy sociālis means “of the allies”: bellum sociāle, the Social War (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Sen. Ep. 95.52: amōrem indidit mūtuum et sociābilēs fēcit
terms.comment: Rare, and not before Augustus (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.21: convīctum hūmānum et societātem

terms.grammar: noun; its genitive does for “social”: societās generis hūmānī, human society
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.54: prīma societās in ipsō conjugiō est
Cic. Amic. 20: societās generis hūmānī (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: inter nōs, quī hominem sociāle animal commūnī bonō genitum vidērī volumus
phrases.english: among us, who would have man seen as a social animal, born for the common good

phrases.latin: beneficium dare sociālis rēs est, aliquem conciliat, aliquem obligat
phrases.english: doing a kindness is a social act: it wins someone over, it puts someone in your debt

phrases.latin: prūdēns simplicitās, parēs amīcī; convīctus facilis, sine arte mēnsa
phrases.english: wise simplicity, friends who are your equals; easy company, a table without fuss

sources: Lewis & Short: socialis · Lewis & Short: sociabilis · Lewis & Short: convictus · Lewis & Short: societas · Lewis & Short: ordo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. class: social class.
